description: WHEN SPACES of the ordered EVALUATE CONFIRMI at app/cbl/COBIL00C.cbl:173-191 - the arm at :182-184 that reads the account and then asks the user to confirm. SERVICE, and the first case in this directory to SEED A DATASET: case01, case02 and case06 touch no file at all and case03 seeds the same fixture row through the controller, so this is where the decoded 300-byte CVACT01Y field map is established for the cases that reuse it. IN SOURCE ORDER, and the order is the behaviour. :156 SET CONF-PAY-NO TO TRUE, before any validation, so CONF-PAY-YES is false for the whole invocation - that single statement is why :210 takes its ELSE. :158-167 EVALUATE TRUE finds ACTIDINI non-blank, so it takes WHEN OTHER / CONTINUE at :165-166: a genuine no-op arm, and no error. :169 IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON opens, and :170-171 MOVE ACTIDINI OF COBIL0AI TO ACCT-ID / XREF-ACCT-ID - one MOVE, two receivers, PIC X(11) into two PIC 9(11) items, with NO NUMERIC VALIDATION ANYWHERE IN THE PROGRAM. None is added here (practice B5): the identifier seeded is eleven digits, so the move is unremarkable, and inventing an edit the source does not perform would be a different program. :173-191 then evaluates CONFIRMI in exact source order - WHEN 'Y' at :174 and WHEN 'y' at :175 do not match, WHEN 'N' at :178 and WHEN 'n' at :179 do not match, WHEN SPACES at :182 MATCHES, and WHEN LOW-VALUES at :183 and WHEN OTHER at :185 are never reached. EVALUATE takes the first matching WHEN and WHEN OTHER is the default, so an implementation that reordered the arms or let one fall through into the next would be a different program (gate G30). Note what this arm does NOT do: unlike :176-177 it does not SET CONF-PAY-YES, and that omission is the whole distinction between a lookup and a payment. THE READ IS ISSUED WITH UPDATE, ON A PATH THAT WRITES NOTHING. :184 performs READ-ACCTDAT-FILE, which at :345-352 is EXEC CICS READ DATASET(WS-ACCTDAT-FILE) INTO(ACCOUNT-RECORD) LENGTH(LENGTH OF ACCOUNT-RECORD) RIDFLD(ACCT-ID) KEYLENGTH(LENGTH OF ACCT-ID) UPDATE RESP(WS-RESP-CD) RESP2(WS-REAS-CD), and the EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD at :355-372 takes its first arm, WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :357, whose body is CONTINUE. In Java that is AccountRepository.readForUpdate and the record is HELD (gate G47, the read-for-update NORMAL arm). Nothing is rewritten afterwards and no ENDBR or release is issued - the lock is simply left to the end of the task. That is the source behaviour and it is preserved, not corrected (practice B5). WS-ACCTDAT-FILE is 'ACCTDAT ' at :41, which is the CICS FILE name the online programs use; the dataset is addressed here by the binding key ACCTDAT that src/main/resources/application-test.yml declares for it, never by a literal dataset name. THE 300-BYTE RECORD, SUMMED FROM app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy RATHER THAN FROM PROSE (practice B11). ACCT-ID 9(11) at 1-11, ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS X(01) at 12, ACCT-CURR-BAL S9(10)V99 at 13-24, ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT at 25-36, ACCT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT at 37-48, ACCT-OPEN-DATE X(10) at 49-58, the misspelled ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE X(10) at 59-68, ACCT-REISSUE-DATE X(10) at 69-78, ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT at 79-90, ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT at 91-102, ACCT-ADDR-ZIP X(10) at 103-112, ACCT-GROUP-ID X(10) at 113-122 and FILLER X(178) at 123-300. That is 300, the RECLN the copybook's own header states (gate G19). ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE IS MISSPELLED IN THE COPYBOOK AT CVACT01Y.cpy:11 AND IS MISSPELLED HERE (requirement I1): correcting it to ACCT-EXPIRATION-DATE would leave the diff looking for a span the decoder never produces, which is a silent parity break rather than a loud one. FILLER X(178) IS PINNED, AS 178 SPACES (gate G21). It is an addressable span and not a gap: omit it and the image is 122 bytes and every offset after it shifts, which is precisely why the complete image is pinned alongside the thirteen named fields. THE OFFSET TRAP, VERIFIED BY SLICING THE FIXTURE RATHER THAN BY READING PROSE ABOUT IT: offsets 103-112 hold 'A000000000' and that span is ACCT-ADDR-ZIP, while ACCT-GROUP-ID at 113-122 holds TEN SPACES. Prose elsewhere describes 'A000000000' as a group-id trailer; it is not, and a case that believed it would pin two fields wrongly while the total width still summed to 300. ZONED DECIMAL, TRUNCATION, AND WHY THE BYTES ARE PINNED AND NOT THE QUANTITY. S9(10)V99 occupies exactly twelve character positions - ten integer digits and two fraction digits - and the sign consumes no position of its own, which is the only reading under which the copybook sums to 300. The sign is overpunched into the TRAILING byte, and in all fifty fixture rows that byte is '{', a positive sign carrying a low-order digit of zero. So the stored image 00000001940{ carries the digits 000000019400, whose first ten are the integer part 0000000194 and whose last two are the fraction 00: the value is 194.00, not 1940.00. The five monetary spans are therefore expected AS THEIR STORED TWELVE-BYTE IMAGES, transcribed from the fixture - 00000001940{ for the balance, 00000020200{ for the 2020.00 credit limit, 00000010200{ for the 1020.00 cash limit and 00000000000{ for each cycle amount, both 0.00. Pinning the image rather than the decimal literal pins the OVERPUNCH BYTE ITSELF: the unsigned form 000000019400 decodes to the same quantity but is not what COBOL writes into a signed DISPLAY item, and a byte-level gate exists to report that difference. Where a quantity is modelled in Java it is a BigDecimal at SCALE 2 with RoundingMode.DOWN and never a double or a float (AAP rules R2 and R4, gate G23): a V-scale scan of all 28 copybooks returns only V99, and the keyword ROUNDED appears zero times in all 28 programs, so truncation toward zero is the only faithful mode - never HALF_UP and never HALF_EVEN. Nothing on this path needs a rounding decision, because no arithmetic runs; the mode is named because the DECODE of a stored span is where a wrong scale would first show. THERE IS NO COMP-3 IN ANY COPYBOOK IN THIS REPOSITORY - verified zero - so no packed-decimal nibble unpacking is involved; the WS-ABS-TIME PIC S9(15) COMP-3 at COBIL00C.cbl:59 is working storage and is never persisted. THE EDITED BALANCE IS A DIFFERENT FIELD FROM THE STORED ONE, AT A DIFFERENT WIDTH. :193 MOVE ACCT-CURR-BAL TO WS-CURR-BAL and :194 MOVE WS-CURR-BAL TO CURBALI OF COBIL0AI sit INSIDE the :169 guard but OUTSIDE the EVALUATE, so they run on every stage-two arm including the ones that have already sent a screen. WS-CURR-BAL is PIC +9999999999.99 at :56 - a sign position, ten integer positions, an actual decimal point character and two fraction positions, which is fourteen bytes and an exact fit for the symbolic map's CURBAL X(14). For 194.00 it renders +0000000194.00: a leading plus because the value is at or above zero, no separators and no zero suppression. This arm is the one path where that move does what it looks like it does, because it is the only arm that both reads the account and does not clear the field first. Do not confuse these fourteen edited characters with the twelve zoned bytes of the record span; they are two representations of one quantity and both are pinned, at their own widths. STAGE THREE PASSES AND STAGE FOUR PROMPTS. :197-206 tests IF ACCT-CURR-BAL <= ZEROS AND ACTIDINI OF COBIL0AI NOT = SPACES AND LOW-VALUES - a conjunction, and the balance just read is 194.00, which is above zero, so the 'You have nothing to pay...' rejection does not fire and no error flag is raised. :208 opens the last guard, :210 IF CONF-PAY-YES is FALSE because :156 set CONF-PAY-NO and :182-184 never changed it, so control reaches the ELSE at :236: :237-238 MOVE 'Confirm to make a bill payment...' TO WS-MESSAGE and :239 MOVE -1 TO CONFIRML OF COBIL0AI. The -1 is CURSOR METADATA and not payload - it is an xxxL length item, which is how COBOL positions the cursor - so it is declared as cursorField rather than as a screen field. Note what is ABSENT from this arm: it sets NO error flag. It is a prompt asking the user to type Y or N, not a rejection, and that difference is exactly why :242 PERFORM SEND-BILLPAY-SCREEN is reached. ONE SEND, AND ITS FOUR FIELDS. :242 is the only send on this path, so the expectation carries exactly one. SEND-BILLPAY-SCREEN at :289-301 performs POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :291, moves the eighty-byte WS-MESSAGE over the seventy-eight-byte ERRMSGO at :293 - the two-byte loss is the picture difference between PIC X(80) and PIC X(78) and not a shortened expectation - and then issues EXEC CICS SEND MAP('COBIL0A') MAPSET('COBIL00') FROM(COBIL0AO) ERASE CURSOR at :295-301. ERRMSGO is therefore the 33-character message left-justified and space-padded to exactly 78. ACTIDINO is the eleven characters as received, CURBALO the fourteen just edited, and CONFIRMO the single space that arrived - unchanged, because no statement on this arm writes it. The four are addressed as xxxO items because app/cpy-bms/COBIL00.CPY:79 declares COBIL0AO REDEFINES COBIL0AI, so the input and the output views are ONE SPAN: a value received in CONFIRMI is observable in CONFIRMO, and :298 sends FROM(COBIL0AO). THE HEADER SIX ARE THE CONTROLLER'S AND ARE DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED HERE. POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :319-338 writes TRNNAME 'CB00', PGMNAME 'COBIL00C', TITLE01 and TITLE02 as app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy:18-22 declares them at their full PIC X(40) width - '      AWS Mainframe Modernization       ' with six leading and seven trailing blanks and '              CardDemo                  ' with fourteen leading and eighteen trailing - and CURDATE and CURTIME as the eight-byte MM/DD/YY and HH:MM:SS groups of app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy, which at this case's pinned instant are 07/19/22 and 23:12:32. Those six carry no decision and are projected by BillPaymentController, not by the service under test here, so a SERVICE case that declared them would be claiming fields its own unit does not write. They are asserted where they belong: case01 and case03 pin all ten items of the map. WHAT DOES NOT HAPPEN, AND WHY THAT IS AN ASSERTION RATHER THAN AN OMISSION. Everything between :211 and :235 is inside IF CONF-PAY-YES and none of it runs: READ-CXACAIX-FILE, MOVE HIGH-VALUES TO TRAN-ID, STARTBR / READPREV / ENDBR-TRANSACT-FILE, the INITIALIZE and the eleven moves that assemble the 350-byte transaction, GET-CURRENT-TIMESTAMP, WRITE-TRANSACT-FILE, the program's single COMPUTE ACCT-CURR-BAL = ACCT-CURR-BAL - TRAN-AMT at :234, and UPDATE-ACCTDAT-FILE at :235. So expectedWrites is EMPTY, which is the positive assertion that nothing was written anywhere - not an absence of interest - and expectedFinalState pins the seeded account row byte for byte to prove the record is still there, unchanged, after a read that held it for update. The dataset-level expectations say the rest: ACCTDAT holds zero rows on the WRITES channel and one on FINAL_STATE, and TRANSACT holds zero on both. Those two zero counts are the only way to state 'the transaction master was reported and produced nothing', because a channel with no row has no row for a row-level expectation to address; each also pins the width that identifies the dataset, 300 for CVACT01Y and 350 for CVTRA05Y. ONLY ACCTDAT IS SEEDED. The cross-reference is read at :421 inside the unreached payment block, so seeding CXACAIX would assert a read this arm does not make, and normalisations is empty as a consequence - the recorded cardxref 36-to-50 filler pad has nothing to apply to, and a normalisation naming a dataset the case does not seed cannot fire. expectedMessages is empty because every DISPLAY in the program - :366, :397, :430, :461, :490 and :541 - sits in a WHEN OTHER arm of a file operation, and this path takes the NORMAL arm of the only file operation it performs. The prompt text is asserted once, as ERRMSGO on the send that produced it, which is where screen text belongs; repeating it on a message channel would claim an emission the program never made. The attribute map is empty and must stay empty: COBIL00C's COPY list at :63-85 is COCOM01Y, COBIL00, COTTL01Y, CSDAT01Y, CSMSG01Y, CVACT01Y, CVACT03Y, CVTRA05Y, DFHAID and DFHBMSCA - NEITHER CSSETATY NOR CSSTRPFY IS COPIED and DFHRED appears nowhere in the program's 572 lines - so there is no red-and-asterisk highlight to expect, and the one attribute byte the program ever writes is the DFHGREEN of :526, on the transaction-WRITE success arm this path never reaches. STATELESSNESS, AND THE CONTEXT STAYS 1. EIBCALEN is 218: the 160 bytes app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy declares for CARDDEMO-COMMAREA plus the 58 bytes of the CDEMO-CB00-INFO group COBIL00C.cbl appends inside the same 01 group. The area arrives with CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT of 1, which is what :112 tests through CDEMO-PGM-REENTER and is the REENTER half of gate G38, and it leaves as 1: no XCTL occurs on this arm, so RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN and its MOVE ZEROS TO CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT at :280 are never reached and the next invocation re-enters again. All sixteen shared spans travel back exactly as they arrived, because no statement on this path writes one. All of it - the area, the AID and the screen values - travels in the payload, so no server-side session state exists or is implied (gate G37, AAP rule R6). DETERMINISM. The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:32, the instant the program's own version footer at :571 carries, and it is the SAME instant every other case in this directory pins; the header date and time are derived from that injected Clock through common/DateHeader and never from a captured now (practice B7). Two-digit month, day and hour, no midnight and no daylight-saving edge, so neither rendering is ambiguous. NO 26-BYTE TIMESTAMP IS PRODUCED ON THIS PATH: GET-CURRENT-TIMESTAMP is performed only at :230, inside the unreached payment block, so nothing here composes TRAN-ORIG-TS or TRAN-PROC-TS. US-ASCII is named explicitly rather than left to a platform default, which for a nine-fixture ASCII corpus and a twelve-dataset EBCDIC one is the difference between a comparison and a coincidence (practice B8). UNIT KIND. SERVICE, driving BillPaymentService.processEnterKey - the real @Service, constructed through its own constructor and called as a plain object, with NO HTTP, no MockMvc, no TestRestTemplate, no servlet container, no JobLauncher and no application context anywhere in the path (gate G51). That is where the decision logic of PROCESS-ENTER-KEY lives, which is exactly why the service split exists and exactly why a parity case must reach it with nothing in between; the unit of work is real, because :351 states the UPDATE option and a record lock outside a unit of work is released before the task that asked for it can rely on it. PROVENANCE. Every value above is STATICALLY DERIVED - read out of app/cbl/COBIL00C.cbl:154-244 and :343-372, cross-checked against the byte layout of app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy, the xxxI PICTURE clauses of app/cpy-bms/COBIL00.CPY and the DFHMDF definitions of app/bms/COBIL00.bms, the X(40) VALUE literals of app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy, the 160-byte layout of app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy, the CB00 transaction and ACCTDAT file definitions of app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD, and row 0 of the real app/data/ASCII/acctdata.txt, which is byte-identical to the shipped src/test/resources/fixtures/acctdata.txt (50 rows of exactly 300 bytes) - and it WAS NOT CAPTURED FROM A LIVE COBOL EXECUTION, not one byte of it. Such a capture is empirically impossible in this environment: no z/OS or CICS runtime, an indexed file handler the available compiler reports as disabled, no Language Environment CEE services, and DFHAID and DFHBMSCA - both copied by this program at :84-85 - absent from the repository, which is why the DFHENTER mnemonic this case declares comes from common/CicsAid, the single reproduction of DFHAID, rather than from a copybook. AAP 0.7.6 documents eight verified blockers, 0.9.11 records the substitution as risk R-A escalated for confirmation rather than absorbed, and 0.9.12 records the missing copybooks as risk R-D. No reference input under app/cbl, app/cpy, app/cpy-bms, app/bms or app/data was modified to make any value here convenient (practice B3): the row was chosen, not edited. GATES. G15 (one of the twenty cases of this program), G16 (seeded from the real acctdata.txt), G18 (the diff count must be zero), G19 (the 300-byte width), G21 (FILLER emitted and space-filled), G23 (scale 2), G30 (EVALUATE CONFIRMI order preserved, WHEN OTHER last), G37 (no server-side state), G38 (the REENTER side), G47 (the READ-ACCTDAT-FILE NORMAL arm) and G51 (reached without HTTP or a JobLauncher). NOT APPLICABLE HERE, AND NOT INVENTED: the CSSETATY DFHRED-and-asterisk highlight, since neither CSSETATY nor CSSTRPFY is copied; G24 and G28, since the single COMPUTE at :234 is not reached; G45, since the CXACAIX finder is not reached; G32, since the program contains no GO TO; G35, since it contains no CALL 'CEE3ABD' and never touches RETURN-CODE, which is why the expected return code is 0; G39, since this screen has no pagination; and G40, since no XCTL occurs. No user rules were provided for this project, so no rule governs this file; the enterprise practices B1, B3, B5, B7, B8, B11 and B12 stand in their place and are honoured above.
